headlines.title: 중동 전쟁도 이긴 반도체의 힘 … K수출 역대급 질주
headlines.summary: 4월 수출 800억弗 돌파 역대 2위 반도체, 13개월 연속 동월 최고치 선박·바이오 늘고 자동차는 줄어 유가 급등에 석유제품 수출액 증가 국민일보DB 중동 전쟁 악재에도 4월 수출이 역대급 실적을 이어갔다. 전년 대비 48% 급증한 859억 달러로 사상 처음으로 두 달 연속 ‘수출 800억 달러 상회’라는 기록을 세웠다.

headlines.title: 韓 수출 두달 연속 800억달러 돌파 … 이대로면 日 제친다
headlines.summary: 4월 수출 127조원… 48% 급증 지난달 우리나라의 수출액이 3월에 이어 다시 한번 800억달러(약 118조원)를 넘어섰다. 중동 전쟁과 미국 관세에도 반도체를 앞세워 역대 최대 호황을 이어가고 있는 것이다. 현재 추세라면 사상 처음으로 우리나라가 연간 수출 규모에서 일본을 추월할 것으로 보인다.

headlines.title: 반도체 질주에 … 4월 수출도 800억 弗 넘었다
headlines.summary: 3월 이어 또 '깜짝 수출' 859억弗 역대 2위 11개월째 수출 신기록 행진 반도체 수출 전년보다 174%↑ 전쟁·관세로 車는 소폭 감소 수입도 두달째 600억弗 넘어 한국 수출이 두 달 연속 800억달러를 넘어섰다. 반도체 수출이 지난해 같은 기간보다 세 배 가까이로 급증해 중동 전쟁의 충격이 본격적으로 반영될 것이란 우려를 씻어냈다.

headlines.title: AI 반도체 수요 지속에 수출 859억弗 역대 2위
headlines.summary: 산업부 4월 수출입 통계 고유가에 에너지수입도 '쑥' 지난 4월 수출액이 전년 동월 대비 48% 증가하며 역대 두 번째로 많은 수치를 기록했다. 반도체 수출액이 1년 새 3배 가까이 넘게 늘며 전체 수출을 이끌었다. 1일 산업통상부는 4월 수출액이 858억9000만달러를 기록하며 지난 3월에 이어 2개월 연속 800억달러를 상회했다고 밝혔다.

key_headlines.title: Virtual Asset Capital Gains Tax at 22% to Be Implemented
key_headlines.summary: South Korea is preparing to end the virtual asset capital gains tax deferral starting in 2027, with the National Tax Service aiming to implement a 22% separate tax system and begin reporting in May 2028. The cryptocurrency industry is concerned about domestic exchange discrimination and potential losses being taxed.

key_headlines.title: Kia Motors Likely to Surpass Hyundai's April Domestic Sales for First Time Since 1998 Group Integration
key_headlines.summary: Kia is expected to exceed Hyundai's monthly domestic sales in April for the first time following the 1998 group merger, aided by component supply disruptions and recall issues affecting Hyundai's Palisade model.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's April Exports Exceed $80 Billion for Second Consecutive Month Amid Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: April exports surged 48% year-on-year to $859 billion, marking historic consecutive months above $80 billion, driven by semiconductor exports hitting a 13-month consecutive record despite Middle East tensions and geopolitical challenges.

key_headlines.title: Inflation Pressures Mount with High Oil Prices, Exchange Rates, and Chip Supply Inflation
key_headlines.summary: South Korea faces renewed inflationary pressures from elevated crude oil prices, weak won exchange rates, and chip inflation, with concerns that consumer price inflation could reaccelerate to 3% starting in the second quarter.

key_headlines.title: LPG Supply Prices Rise Up to 11% in May Amid Middle East Tensions
key_headlines.summary: Domestic LPG prices increased up to 11% in May with propane rising 140 won per kilogram in just one month due to Middle East conflict driving up global LPG import prices.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy shows mixed signals with remarkable export performance but rising inflation concerns. April exports reached a record $859 billion with semiconductors leading the surge, marking the second consecutive month above $80 billion. However, inflation pressures are mounting from elevated crude oil prices breaching $126 per barrel, weak won exchange rates, and chip supply inflation, potentially pushing consumer price inflation back above 3% in the second quarter. The government faces challenges balancing growth support with price stability amid ongoing Middle East tensions creating commodity market volatility.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea faces mounting pressure to implement interest rate increases, with securities analysts expecting two rate hikes during 2026, potentially in August and November, driven by positive production gaps and accommodative financial conditions. The European Central Bank also held rates steady while expressing concerns about potential stagflation recurrence similar to 1970s oil shocks. South Korea's 1Q real GDP growth posted 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, supporting arguments for monetary tightening, while the government grapples with fiscal challenges including elevated national tax burdens and considerations for virtual asset taxation reforms. March current account surplus is expected to set new records driven by semiconductor export strength.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI index surged past 6,700 before pulling back to the 6,600 level, driven by semiconductor strength but pressured by high crude oil prices and Federal Reserve's continued rate hold at 3.5%. New leveraged ETFs for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix were launched to meet investor demand, while securities company reports proliferated as trading volumes exceeded 3 trillion won annually. Improved corporate earnings prospects and dividend payouts lifted target prices for brokerages like Kium Securities, reflecting market enthusiasm tempered by international rate hold decisions and geopolitical uncertainties.
sections.Industry & Technology: Semiconductor exports achieved record performance with 13 consecutive months of year-over-year highs, while LG Energy Solution secured a 10 trillion won battery supply contract with BMW for electric vehicles, signaling recovery in Korean secondary battery sector. Lithium deposits sufficient for approximately 130 million electric vehicles were discovered in the United States, potentially reducing import dependencies for global EV production. Green energy technology development continues with companies exploring solar power systems as alternatives to existing power generation methods, while NAND flash memory rebounded as a key AI inference component, elevating its significance beyond storage applications.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment sales increasingly shift toward monthly rentals, with monthly rental transactions exceeding 70% of total housing transactions as jeonse (long-term lease) housing becomes scarce. Apartment prices in Seoul surged with some properties rising from 1.4 billion won to 1.7 billion won, attracting first-time homebuyers and fueling market volatility. The government is reviewing inclusion of jeonse diagnostic prices in the real transaction disclosure system to prevent deep-loss jeonse situations, while political candidates debate housing supply policies amid ongoing jeonse crisis concerns and rental market imbalances.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.5% with growing internal dissent, featuring the largest number of dissenting votes since 1992, with some policymakers pushing for rate cuts. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell indicated he would remain on the Fed's board after his chairman term ends, citing unresolved political pressures and Trump administration investigations into Federal Reserve operations. Markets showed mixed performance with the Nasdaq marginally rising 0.04% amid crude oil price surges and persistent uncertainty over Fed policy direction, while Powell warned of unprecedented economic challenges from supply shocks that could simultaneously raise inflation and unemployment.
sections.AI & Economy: The AI market is transitioning from pure intelligence competition toward efficiency and profitability competition, with investors increasingly favoring cost-effective AI solutions over merely sophisticated models. CPU-related stocks gained attention as AI agent demand grows, shifting focus from GPU and memory semiconductor dominance as on-device AI PCs accelerate adoption. The government launched national growth funds emphasizing AI and semiconductor investments to diversify from previous low-yield policy fund returns, while Huawei positions itself to dominate China's AI chip market through partnerships with foundry SMIC, addressing U.S. export restrictions on advanced semiconductors.
sections.Others: U.S. low-cost carrier Spirit Airlines failed to secure emergency government rescue financing from the Trump administration, facing imminent operation suspension. NAND flash memory revival continues as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix accelerate advanced process conversion, elevating NAND as crucial to AI inference and AI data centers. Venture capital funding concentrates on promising AI technology startups with multiple seed investments, while counterfeit currency operations demonstrate emerging digital fraud risks with one defendant sentenced for printing fake banknotes using consumer-grade color printers.
